Therefore, when adjudicating disputes over foreign guarantee contracts provided by wholly foreign-owned enterprises as guarantors, it is still necessary to examine whether the foreign guarantee has been registered with the foreign exchange administration authority; if not registered, it shall be deemed invalid.

full_text_en:
Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited, Shanghai Branch v. Jingxuan Hotel (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. and Wanxuan Property Co., Ltd. — dispute over a financial loan contract

Ruling Summary

Article 6(1) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China clearly provides that an external guarantee contract is invalid if it has not been approved or registered by the competent state authority. According to the relevant provisions of the Measures for the Administration of External Guarantees by Domestic Institutions, although external guarantees provided by wholly foreign-owned enterprises do not require individual approval, they still need to be registered. Therefore, when trying a dispute involving an external guarantee contract provided by a wholly foreign-owned enterprise as the guarantor, it is still necessary to examine whether the external guarantee it provided has been registered with the foreign exchange administration authority. If it is not registered, it shall be deemed invalid.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2010) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 12

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Jingxuan Hotel (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. Domicile: Huayi Design Center Building, Caitian Road, Futian District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province. Contact Address: No. 277 Fuhua Road, Futian District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Li Yinkun, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Cao Qiang, male, Han nationality, born in 1978, Administrative Manager of Jingxuan Hotel (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., residing in Luohu District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited, Shanghai Branch. Domicile: Room 13-042, 13/F, HSBC Tower, 1000 Lujiazui Ring Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

Person in Charge: Gan Kunliang, Branch Manager.

Agent ad litem: Wang Zheng, lawyer of Shanghai Hongqiao Zhenghan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Chen Jinlong, lawyer of Shanghai Hongqiao Zhenghan Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Wanxuan Property Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room B, 14/F, Wahyin Commercial Centre, 383 Hennessy Road, Wanchai, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Legal Representative: Li Yinkun.

The appellant, Jingxuan Hotel (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jingxuan Company), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2009) Hu Gao Min Si (Shang) Chu Zi No. 2 rendered by the Shanghai High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Shanghai High Court) on February 8, 2010, in the case of the dispute over a financial loan contract with the respondent, Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited, Shanghai Branch (hereinafter referred to as HSBC Shanghai Branch), and the defendant at first instance, Wanxuan Property Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Wanxuan Property), filed an appeal to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Zhang Guorong, and Judges Ren Xuefeng and Song Jianli, and held a public hearing of this case on October 19, 2010. The agent ad litem of Jingxuan Company, Cao Qiang, and the agents ad litem of HSBC Shanghai Branch, Zhong Renjian and Wang Zheng, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. Wanxuan Property, having been served with a summons by this Court, failed to appear in court without justifiable reasons. After the hearing in this Court, HSBC Shanghai Branch revoked its authorization for lawyer Zhong Renjian and re-appointed lawyer Chen Jinlong as its agent. Because the trial of this case had to be based on the outcome of the case of Yang Juntai v. Shenzhen Branch of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange concerning external guarantee registration, which was being tried by the Luohu District People's Court of Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province, this Court issued a civil ruling (2010) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 12 on November 4, 2010, suspending the trial of this case. The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province rendered a final administrative ruling (2011) Shen Zhong Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 352 on August 2, 2011, and that administrative case has been concluded. This Court notified all parties on September 2, 2011, that the litigation in this case had been resumed. On October 31, 2011, this Court again notified all parties to produce evidence for verification. The agent ad litem of Jingxuan Company, Cao Qiang, and the agents ad litem of HSBC Shanghai Branch, Wang Zheng and Chen Jinlong, appeared in court and presented opinions on evidence verification. Wanxuan Property, having been served with a summons by this Court, failed to appear in court for evidence verification without justifiable reasons. This case is now concluded.

HSBC Shanghai Branch filed a complaint with the Shanghai High Court, alleging that: On April 23, 1997, Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited, Shenzhen Branch (hereinafter referred to as HSBC Shenzhen Branch) and Wanxuan Property signed a bank facility letter, agreeing that HSBC Shenzhen Branch would provide Wanxuan Property with a facility of a maximum term loan not exceeding HKD 150,000,000 and an overdraft facility of HKD 45,000,000. The bank facility letter also stipulated terms on interest, fees, drawdown methods, repayment methods, guarantee, and other matters. After the bank facility letter was signed, HSBC Shenzhen Branch, in accordance with Wanxuan Property's instructions, issued the corresponding loans as agreed. However, Wanxuan Property failed to repay the loans in a timely manner as stipulated in the relevant loan letters. As of May 31, 2009 (inclusive), Wanxuan Property still owed loan principal of HKD 118,354,000 and loan interest of HKD 64,346,398.72. On May 20, 1998, HSBC Shenzhen Branch and Jingxuan Company entered into a Property Mortgage Contract (I) notarized by Shenzhen Notary Public Office; on September 25, 1998, they entered into a Property Mortgage Contract (II) notarized by Shenzhen Notary Public Office; and on November 15, 2002, they entered into a Property Mortgage Confirmation Contract notarized by Shenzhen Notary Public Office. They agreed that Jingxuan Company would provide mortgage guarantee for the above loans, and the collateral was the 1st to 11th floors and 13th to 30th floors of the Jingxuan Hotel owned by Jingxuan Company. The above mortgage contracts have been registered with the Shenzhen Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources and Housing Administration, and the external guarantee has been registered with the Shenzhen Branch of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. HSBC Shenzhen Branch was originally a branch of the foreign bank Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (hereinafter referred to as HSBC) in mainland China. Later, HSBC underwent restructuring, after which HSBC established a separate legal person in mainland China, and all its original branches were cancelled except for HSBC Shanghai Branch. Therefore, the credit and guarantee business in dispute in this case has been naturally transferred to HSBC Shanghai Branch, which is the same legal entity, and HSBC Shanghai Branch retained the accounts for Wanxuan Property. Based on the above facts, Wanxuan Property's failure to repay the loans constituted a breach of contract and should bear corresponding liability. Jingxuan Company, as the guarantor, should also bear corresponding guarantee liability. Accordingly, HSBC Shanghai Branch requested the court to order: 1. Wanxuan Property to repay to HSBC Shanghai Branch the loan principal of HKD 118,354,000 and the loan interest (as of May 31, 2009 (inclusive), HKD 64,346,398.72, and calculated until the date of actual payment, at an annual interest rate of the Hong Kong dollar prime rate plus 4%); 2. Wanxuan Property to compensate HSBC Shanghai Branch for the lawyer's fees of RMB 100,000 incurred for this case; 3. Wanxuan Property and Jingxuan Company to bear all litigation costs including the case acceptance fee and preservation fee; 4. HSBC Shanghai Branch to have a priority right to be repaid from the 1st to 11th floors and 13th to 30th floors of the Jingxuan Hotel located at the southwest corner of the intersection of Caitian Road and Fuhua Road in Shenzhen City, owned by Jingxuan Company, and to order Jingxuan Company to convert the collateral into money by sale by auction or otherwise, and to satisfy HSBC Shanghai Branch's claims under items 1, 2, and 3 above on a priority basis from the proceeds of the disposal.

The Shanghai High Court found the following facts upon trial: On April 23, 1997, HSBC Shenzhen Branch issued a bank facility letter to Wanxuan Property, stating that we agree to grant your company a bank facility, and agree to grant your company such facility under the specific terms and conditions described in this facility letter, after the following guarantee has been completed in a manner satisfactory to us. Specific contents: Lender: HSBC Shenzhen Branch. Borrower: Wanxuan Property. Facility/Amount: (A) Term loan not exceeding HKD 150,000,000, (B) Overdraft facility of HKD 45,000,000. Purpose: To meet the working capital needs of the borrower's various investments. Loan term: (A) Approximately 4.5 years, subject to our annual review, (B) Subject to annual review and renewal. Interest: Interest on the term loan and overdraft facility under this facility letter shall be charged at the Hong Kong dollar prime rate plus 1% per annum (current Hong Kong dollar prime rate is 8.75% per annum, we have the right to determine the interest rate fluctuation). Interest will be deducted monthly from the borrower's account opened with us. Guarantee: 1. Mortgage on the entire first to third floors of the Shenzhen Futian District Prosperity Garden Building, with Shenzhen Kaishi Investment Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Kaishi Company) as the mortgagor, i.e., this first priority mortgage guarantees the borrower's occasional debts under general bank facilities, including future loans, for which the borrower and the mortgagor assume unlimited liability. 2. Letter of undertaking, undertaking that Wanxuan Property will mortgage to us a hotel to be acquired in Shenzhen Futian District within nine months after the first drawdown. 3. Personal guarantee of HKD 195,000,000 provided by Mr. Li Yinkun. 4. Letter of undertaking issued by Kaishi Company, undertaking to directly use all rental income from the Prosperity Garden Building to repay the loan. ... Governing law: The loan documents are governed by Hong Kong law and subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of Hong Kong courts, while the land and property mortgage are governed by PRC law. Please arrange for your authorized signatory to sign a copy of this facility letter in accordance with the terms of the power of attorney provided to us, and return it to us, indicating your understanding and acceptance of all terms and conditions of this facility. The bank facility letter also stipulated matters concerning drawdown, repayment, commitment fee, arrangement fee, prepayment, and others. Li Yinkun, the legal representative of Wanxuan Property, signed and affixed the seal on this bank facility letter.

On April 30 and May 3, 1997, HSBC Shenzhen Branch, upon the application of Wanxuan Property, disbursed HKD 78,000,000 and HKD 35,000,000 respectively to Wanxuan Property's loan account.

On August 11, 1997, HSBC Shenzhen Branch issued a bank facility letter to Li Yinkun, the legal representative of Wanxuan Property, stating that the bank agreed to allow the use of HKD 7,800,000 (equivalent to USD 1,000,000) as an import facility within the original overdraft facility of HKD 45,000,000. Li Yinkun signed and affixed the seal on this bank facility letter.

On August 12 and November 12, 1997, HSBC Shenzhen Branch, upon the application of Wanxuan Property, disbursed HKD 25,000,000 and HKD 12,000,000 respectively to the above loan account of Wanxuan Property.

On May 20, 1998, HSBC Shenzhen Branch, Jingxuan Company, and Wanxuan Property entered into a Property Mortgage Contract stipulating that the mortgagee is HSBC Shenzhen Branch, the mortgagor is Jingxuan Company (formerly known as Huaxiang Real Estate Development (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd.), and the borrower is Wanxuan Property; Recitals (A)... (B) The mortgagor is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the borrower, owning and operating an investment project tentatively named "Huayi Design Center Building" at the intersection of Caitian Road and Fuhua Road in Futian District, Shenzhen City. (C) Pursuant to a Letter of Undertaking dated April 28, 1997, executed by the borrower, the borrower unconditionally and irrevocably undertakes that within nine months from the date of loan disbursement, the mortgagor shall grant the mortgagee a first priority mortgage on the properties listed in Schedule 1 to this contract, namely the first to eleventh floors and the fifteenth to thirtieth floors of Jingxuan Hotel, as additional security for the repayment of the loan under the loan contract. The mortgagee agrees to accept the mortgaged property from the mortgagor as another collateral for the loan under the loan contract. Upon agreement among the three parties, this contract is hereby concluded and shall be complied with. Article 1, Repayment of the loan: 1. The borrower hereby promises and undertakes to the mortgagee to repay all loans under the loan contract in accordance with the loan contract terms, in the specified amounts and manner, and within the stipulated time, and to perform all obligations under the loan contract. 2. If any of the following circumstances occur, the mortgagee has the right, under lawful premises, to dispose of the mortgaged property in any form, and shall not be liable for any losses arising from the proper exercise of the above rights or powers: 1) The borrower breaches any term of the loan contract, including failure to repay the loan as stipulated in the loan contract; 2) The mortgagor and/or the borrower breaches any term of this contract; ... Article 8, Applicable law and dispute resolution: 1. This contract is entered into under the laws of the People's Republic of China and is protected by the laws of the People's Republic of China. 2. This contract is subject to the relevant provisions of China's real estate management. Other clauses of the contract also stipulated matters concerning property mortgage and insurance, fees and expenses, nature of guarantee and non-waiver, representations and warranties of the mortgagor and borrower, etc. Gao Yuehua signed on behalf of the mortgagee HSBC Shenzhen Branch and affixed the official seal. Li Yinkun signed on behalf of the mortgagor Jingxuan Company and the borrower Wanxuan Property respectively and affixed the official seals of both companies. The following day, the Shenzhen Notary Public Office notarized the above Property Mortgage Contract.

On May 21, 1998, Jingxuan Company issued a Mortgage Declaration stating that this company, regarding the matter of mortgaging its own property for the borrower Wanxuan Property's loan of HKD 195,000,000 from the lender HSBC Shenzhen Branch, voluntarily mortgages to the lender the properties located at Huayi Design Center Building, Caitian Road, Futian District, Shenzhen City, valued at HKD 265,000,000, with property right certificate numbers 3000002151 to 3000002166, 0104227 to 0104237, as security for the borrower's repayment of the above loan. ... This company guarantees that, as the owner of the mortgaged property, it will perform the obligations set for the mortgaged property under the loan contract signed between the borrower and the lender for the above loan, and undertakes that if the borrower fails to repay the loan principal and interest, the lender has the right, in accordance with Article 89(2) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and other relevant legal provisions, to convert the mortgaged property into money or to have priority in repayment from the proceeds of the sale of the mortgaged property for the debts owed by the borrower to the lender. ... On the same day, the Shenzhen Notary Public Office notarized the above Mortgage Declaration. The Futian Branch of the Shenzhen Municipal Bureau of Planning and Land registered the above property mortgage, with mortgage number (98) Shen Fu Fang Ya Zi No. 492.

On September 25, 1998, HSBC Shenzhen Branch, as the mortgagee, and Jingxuan Company, as the mortgagor, entered into a Property Mortgage Contract, with a special statement on the first page that the clauses relating to the borrower are currently not applicable. In the recitals of the contract: ... (D) Pursuant to a Property Mortgage Contract dated May 20, 1998, executed by the mortgagee, the mortgagor, and the borrower, the mortgagor has already mortgaged the first to eleventh floors and the fifteenth to thirtieth floors of the project to the mortgagee. Now the mortgagor further mortgages the thirteenth and fourteenth floors of the project as the collateral under this contract to the mortgagee, granting the mortgagee a first priority mortgage. The other clauses of this contract are consistent with the contents of the Property Mortgage Contract signed on May 20, 1998. Gao Yuehua signed on behalf of the mortgagee HSBC Shenzhen Branch, and Cui Ming signed on behalf of the mortgagor Jingxuan Company, and the official seals of both companies were affixed to the contract. Jingxuan Company, as the mortgagor, also issued a Mortgage Declaration stating that the company voluntarily mortgaged to the lender the properties located on the thirteenth and fourteenth floors of Huayi Design Center Building, Caitian Road, Futian District, Shenzhen City (building area 1,616.32 square meters, property right certificate numbers 3000009313, 3000009314), as security for the borrower's repayment of the above loan. Other contents are consistent with the Mortgage Declaration issued by the above mortgagor on May 21, 1998. On the same day, the Shenzhen Notary Public Office notarized the Property Mortgage Contract and the Mortgage Declaration. On September 28, 1998, the Futian Branch of the Shenzhen Municipal Bureau of Planning and Land registered the above property mortgage, with mortgage number (98) Shen Fu Fang Ya Zi No. 1144.

On October 12, 1998, HSBC Shenzhen Branch issued a bank facility letter to Wanxuan Property, stating that the bank agreed to renew the facility within the following revised limits: The original overdraft facility was HKD 45,000,000, and the current overdraft balance is HKD 40,007,945.71, the overdraft limit is only equivalent to the current overdraft balance, and no further drawdowns will be allowed. The current term loan balance is HKD 150,000,000, ... Repayment: 5 installments, once every six months, from April 30, 1999 to April 30, 2001. As security for the aforementioned facility, the bank will continue to hold: ... 2. Mortgage on the Jingxuan Hotel project located in Shenzhen Futian District. 3. Personal guarantee of HKD 195,000,000 provided by Mr. Li Yinkun on April 28, 1997. ... Li Yinkun, the legal representative of Wanxuan Property, signed and affixed the seal on this bank facility letter.

On June 14, 2002, HSBC Shenzhen Branch issued a bank facility letter to Wanxuan Property, stating: Following recent discussions with your company, we hereby notify your company that we have restructured your company's current total overdraft and loan balance of HKD 126,337,945.71 into a term loan facility under the following terms and conditions. Lender: HSBC Shenzhen Branch. Borrower: Wanxuan Property. Facility/Amount: Restructured term loan, not exceeding HKD 126,337,000. Term: 5 years. Interest shall be charged at the Hong Kong dollar prime rate plus 2% per annum, the bank has the right to determine interest rate fluctuation, and interest shall be deducted from your company's account as agreed. Repayment: Quarterly installments starting from September 30, 2002, with 20 installments. Please note that the above new interest rate shall take effect retroactively only if your company timely and fully pays the first installment of the restructured loan; otherwise, penalty interest will continue to be charged at the current overdue rate. As security for the aforementioned facility, the bank will continue to hold: 1) Mortgage on Jingxuan Hotel in Shenzhen Futian District, with Jingxuan Company as the mortgagor, i.e., this first priority mortgage guarantees the borrower's occasional debts under general bank facilities, including future loans, for which the borrower and the mortgagor assume joint and several unlimited liability. 2) Personal guarantee of HKD 195,000,000 provided by Mr. Li Yinkun on April 28, 1997. 3) Letter of undertaking dated April 28, 1997, issued by Kaishi Company, undertaking to directly use all rental income from the Prosperity Garden Building to repay the loan. 4) Subordinated debt acknowledgment agreement dated April 28, 1997. Wanxuan Property affixed its seal on this facility letter and Li Yinkun signed to confirm.

On November 15, 2002, HSBC Shenzhen Branch, as mortgagee, entered into the Property Mortgage Confirmation Contract with the mortgagor Jingxuan Company and the borrower Wanxuan Properties, stipulating as follows: Recitals: (A) Pursuant to a letter issued by HSBC to the borrower on April 23, 1997 (as supplemented and amended by a letter issued by HSBC to the borrower on August 11, 1997) (hereinafter referred to as the Loan Agreement), and upon the borrower's signed acceptance of the conditions set forth in the Loan Agreement, HSBC agreed to extend a bank loan to the borrower through its Shenzhen Branch. (B) Pursuant to the Loan Agreement: (1) On May 20, 1998, the mortgagee, the mortgagor, and the borrower entered into a Property Mortgage Contract, whereby the mortgagor mortgaged to the mortgagee the 1st to 11th floors and the 15th to 30th floors of Jingxuan Hotel, located at the southwest corner of the intersection of Caitian Road and Fuhua Road, Futian District, Shenzhen City, China; (2) On September 25, 1998, the mortgagee and the mortgagor entered into a Property Mortgage Contract, whereby the mortgagor mortgaged to the mortgagee the 13th and 14th floors of Jingxuan Hotel, located at the southwest corner of the intersection of Caitian Road and Fuhua Road, Futian District, Shenzhen City, China; in order to secure the borrower's repayment of the loan to the mortgagee (such mortgaged properties are hereinafter collectively referred to as the Mortgaged Properties, and such property mortgage contracts are hereinafter collectively referred to as the Mortgage Contracts). (C) Pursuant to a letter issued by HSBC to the borrower on June 14, 2002 (hereinafter referred to as the Supplemental Agreement), and upon the borrower's signed acceptance of the conditions set forth in the Supplemental Agreement, HSBC agreed to restructure the borrower's outstanding indebtedness into a term loan of HKD 126,337,000, with conditions including: the mortgagor and the borrower must separately enter into this Contract to confirm that each Mortgage Contract remains valid and applies to secure the borrower's performance of its obligations and responsibilities under the Loan Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement. Through negotiation among the parties, this Contract is hereby executed, and the parties confirm and hereby agree as follows:

Article 1: Amendments to the Mortgage Contracts
1.1 The Recital (A) of each Mortgage Contract is replaced by the following: "(A) Pursuant to a letter issued by HSBC to the borrower (i.e., the borrower) on April 23, 1997 (as supplemented and amended by a letter issued by HSBC to the borrower on August 11, 1997, and another letter issued on June 14, 2002) (hereinafter referred to as the Loan Contract), and upon the borrower's signed acceptance of the conditions set forth in the Loan Contract, HSBC agreed to extend to the borrower, through its Shenzhen Branch (i.e., the mortgagee, the lender), a term loan in the amount of HKD 126,337,000 (HK$126,337,000) in accordance with the terms of the Loan Contract, as working capital for the borrower's other investment projects. The loan term is fixed at five years as stipulated in the Loan Contract." The Recital (B) of the Irrevocable Power of Attorney in Schedule (IV) of each Mortgage Contract is replaced by the following: "(B) Pursuant to a letter issued by HSBC to Wanxuan Properties (hereinafter referred to as the borrower) on April 23, 1997 (as supplemented and amended by a letter issued by HSBC to the borrower on August 11, 1997, and another letter issued on June 14, 2002) (hereinafter referred to as the Loan Contract), and upon the borrower's signed acceptance of the conditions set forth in the Loan Contract, HSBC agreed to extend to the borrower, through its Shenzhen Branch (i.e., the authorized person), a term loan in the amount of HKD 126,337,000 (HK$126,337,000) in accordance with the terms of the Loan Contract."
1.2 Except for the amendments set forth above, all terms and conditions of each Mortgage Contract shall remain in full force and effect.

Article 2: Confirmation of Mortgage
2.1 The mortgagor and the borrower hereby confirm and affirm to the mortgagee as follows: (i) They have reviewed and agreed to the form and content of the Supplemental Agreement; (ii) Each representation and warranty set forth in Article 5 of each Mortgage Contract remains true and correct as of the date of execution of this Contract, as if each such representation and warranty were made anew on the date of execution of this Contract; (iii) No event of default as described in Article 1, Paragraph 2 or Article 2, Paragraph 5, Subparagraph 7 of any Mortgage Contract has occurred prior to or on the date of execution of this Contract; (iv) Each Mortgage Contract remains in full force and effect, and the Mortgaged Properties continue to be mortgaged to the mortgagee to secure the borrower's and the mortgagor's compliance with and performance of their obligations, duties, and commitments under the Loan Agreement, the Mortgage Contracts, and the Supplemental Agreement.
2.2 This Contract is a document supplemental to each Mortgage Contract. The parties to this Contract confirm that, except as otherwise amended, supplemented, or provided by this Contract with respect to the Mortgage Contracts, all terms and conditions of each Mortgage Contract shall remain in full force and effect. If any provision in any Mortgage Contract conflicts with any provision of this Contract, such provision shall no longer apply or shall be modified as the case may be.
2.3 From the date of execution of this Contract, each Mortgage Contract and this Contract shall constitute one document.
...
The formation, validity, interpretation, performance, and dispute resolution of this Contract shall be governed by the laws of China.

On the same day, the Shenzhen Notary Public Office notarized the Property Mortgage Confirmation Contract: It is hereby certified that the mortgagee, HSBC Shenzhen Branch, represented by its legal representative Ou Shengqin, the mortgagor, Jingxuan Company, represented by its representative Gao Lihui, and the borrower, Wanxuan Properties, represented by its legal representative Li Yinkun, signed the foregoing Property Mortgage Confirmation Contract in Shenzhen on November 15, 2002. The signing behavior of the three parties complies with the provisions of Article 55 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, the content of the contract complies with the provisions of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, and the signatures and seals of the three parties on the contract are genuine.

On March 30, 2007, HSBC issued a Notice to Wanxuan Properties entitled "Further Notice Regarding Transfer of Credit Facilities to and Retention at HSBC Bank (China) Company Limited, Shanghai Branch", stating: Effective April 1, 2007, the following retained credit facilities and retained accounts provided by our Shenzhen Branch to your company will be transferred to and retained at the Retaining Branch (i.e., HSBC Bank (China) Company Limited, Shanghai Branch), and will not be transferred to HSBC Bank (China) Company Limited or any of its branches or sub-branches as a result of the restructuring and business transfer notice. Retained Credit Facility: On June 14, 2002, our branch extended a restructured loan of HKD 126,337,000 to your company, with a term of 5 years, repayable in 20 installments commencing September 30, 2002, together with all amendments, supplements, renewals, extensions, etc. Retained Account: Opening bank: HSBC Bank (China) Company Limited, Shanghai Branch; Account name: Wanxuan Properties Limited.

On the same day, HSBC issued a Notice to Jingxuan Company entitled "Notice Regarding Restructuring and Business Transfer of Mainland China Branches of The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited", stating: Effective April 1, 2007, as the credit facilities provided by the relevant HSBC Mainland China branch and covered by the following mortgage guarantees issued by your company are transferred to the Retaining Branch (i.e., HSBC Bank (China) Company Limited, Shanghai Branch), any and all rights of the relevant HSBC Mainland China branch under such mortgage guarantees are transferred to the Retaining Branch. Your company executed two Property Mortgage Contracts on May 20, 1998 and September 25, 1998, and a Property Mortgage Confirmation Contract on November 15, 2002, agreeing to provide mortgage guarantees for HSBC's credit facility of HKD 195,000,000 (HKD195,000,000) to Wanxuan Properties Limited and the corresponding claims, with the mortgaged property being the 1st-11th floors and 13th-30th floors of Jingxuan Hotel, located at No. 227 Fuhua Road (near Caitian Road), Futian District, Shenzhen.

On November 20, 2008, the Shenzhen Branch of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange issued a Notice of Approval for Capital Account Foreign Exchange Business (No. [2008] 040) in response to Jingxuan Company's application, regarding the approval of supplementary registration of external guarantee: Pursuant to the reply of the Capital Account Department of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (Fa Zi [2008] No. 468), the following is hereby approved: 1. Approval is granted for your company to go through the supplementary registration procedures for external guarantee. The principal and interest of the main debt under the guarantee total HKD 169,000,000. The guaranteed party is Hong Kong Wanxuan Properties Limited, and the beneficiary is HSBC Bank (China) Company Limited, Shanghai Branch. Your company shall come to our branch to go through the supplementary registration procedures within 15 working days from receipt of this document. 2. Your company failed to go through the guarantee registration procedures with the local foreign exchange bureau when providing the external guarantee, which violates the provisions of Article 39 of the Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Measures for the Administration of External Guarantees by Domestic Institutions. Our branch hereby gives a warning to your company for this violation in accordance with Article 50 of the said Detailed Rules. 3. Your company shall conduct business in strict compliance with foreign exchange management regulations in the future. This approval is made in duplicate, the first copy to be retained by the handling department (Capital Account Department), and the second copy to be retained by the domestic investment entity.

On October 8, 2008, HSBC Shanghai Branch issued a Loan Collection Letter to Wanxuan Properties entitled "Loan Collection Letter for Wanxuan Properties Limited", stating: Pursuant to the Loan Letter signed by our bank and your company on April 23, 1997, the First Supplemental Loan Letter signed on August 11, 1997, the Second Supplemental Loan Letter signed on October 12, 1998, and the Third Supplemental Loan Letter signed on June 14, 2002 (hereinafter collectively referred to as the Loan Letter[s]), as of the time of signing the Third Supplemental Loan Letter, the outstanding principal balance of our bank's loan to your company was HKD 126,337,000. Since your company failed to repay the loan principal and interest on the maturity date as stipulated in the Loan Letter, our bank issued loan collection letters to your company on September 21, 2004, March 21, 2006, and March 30, 2007. As of October 8, 2008, your company still owes our bank loan principal of HKD 118,354,000 and related interest of HKD 57,336,389.93. Until the indebtedness is fully repaid, our bank will continue to accrue interest and calculate interest at the default interest rate of 2% per annum in addition to the loan base rate stipulated in the Loan Letter (our bank's Hong Kong dollar prime rate plus 2% per annum) (currently our bank's Hong Kong dollar prime rate is 5.25% per annum). Pursuant to the Loan Letter, our bank again requests your company to immediately and fully repay the above amounts and other amounts payable to our bank under the Loan Letter. Otherwise, our bank will, without further notice to your company, take all appropriate actions to enforce any rights granted under the Loan Letter. ... Our bank has the right to exercise all rights, powers, and remedies conferred by law and the Loan Letter, and to take any action our bank deems appropriate without further notice to your company, including filing a lawsuit against your company. The Shanghai High People's Court also found that: On December 23, 2009, lawyer Dong Guangxian of Johnson Stokes & Master, Hong Kong, issued a legal opinion regarding the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region applicable to this dispute, providing the following Hong Kong law:

1. Hong Kong law affirms the principle of freedom of contract. The Hong Kong Supreme Court applied the principle of freedom of contract in the case of Credit Base (HK) Limited v BBDO Hong Kong Limited (A652/1992), pointing out that once a contract is agreed upon by both parties, it shall be complied with immediately by the parties, and the court will not readily discharge the contract on the grounds that its terms are unreasonable or unfavorable to the performing party. Section 24 of the Hong Kong Money Lenders Ordinance: Prohibition of excessive interest rates (1) Any person (whether a money lender or not) who lends money or offers to lend money at an effective interest rate exceeding 60% per annum commits an offence. (2) Any agreement for the repayment of a loan or for the payment of interest on a loan, and any security provided in respect of such agreement or loan, shall not be enforceable if the effective interest rate exceeds the rate specified in subsection (1).

3. In paragraph 51 of the judgment of the Hong Kong Court of Final Appeal in Bank of China (H.K.) Limited v. Fung Chin Kan & Others (FACV 16/2001), Justice Litton stated: "When a person signs a legal document, he is bound by the terms of that document." This opinion was affirmed in the Chinese judgment of Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited v. Hanlin Electronics Group Co., Ltd. (HCMP 337/2002).
